result.topic_en: Opening page of Euler's prize essay on the physical cause of the ebb and flow of the sea, beginning Chapter I with the general principle that every change of motion in bodies arises either from conservation of motion or from forces, not from occult qualities.
result.transcription:
INQUISITIO PHYSICA
IN CAUSAM
FLUXUS AC REFLUXUS
MARIS.

CAPUT PRIMUM.
De Causa Fluxus ac Refluxus Maris in genere.

§. 1. OMNEM mutationem, quæ in corporibus evenit, vel ab ipsa motûs conservatione proficisci, vel à viribus motum generantibus, hoc quidem tempore, quo qualitates occultæ causæque imaginariæ penitùs sunt explosæ, nulla indiget probatione.
Hoc autem discrimen quovis oblato Phænomeno diligentissimè considerari oportet, ne tam motûs conservationi ejusmodi effectus tribuatur, qui sine viribus oriri nequit, quàm vires investigentur, quæ motum
Gg iij

items.quote: OMNEM mutationem, quæ in corporibus evenit, vel ab ipsa motûs conservatione proficisci, vel à viribus motum generantibus, hoc quidem tempore, quo qualitates occultæ causæque imaginariæ penitùs sunt explosæ, nulla indiget probatione.
items.english: That every change occurring in bodies proceeds either from the very conservation of motion or from forces generating motion needs no proof at this time, when occult qualities and imaginary causes have been entirely rejected.

items.quote: Hoc autem discrimen quovis oblato Phænomeno diligentissimè considerari oportet, ne tam motûs conservationi ejusmodi effectus tribuatur, qui sine viribus oriri nequit, quàm vires investigentur, quæ motum
items.english: This distinction must be considered most carefully for any phenomenon presented, lest an effect that cannot arise without forces be attributed to the conservation of motion, or forces be sought which [the text continues on the next page].
